### AbhinavDasari-pennstate__fog-of-war-mech 5162586 11-20 23:53
economy.py: loot and rest after a confirmed kill
After a kill, walk to the victim's pile (visible cubes within 10 m of where it
fell, else the spot) for at most 6 s, without boosting; skip it when the pile
is over 70 m away, near the zone edge, on another height, by a drone or a
tracked mech. Then rest up to 8 s inside the zone: no new fire (a charging
laser keeps its trigger), ending at 85% HP. Contact ends both: a hit taken
after the kill, or one of the nearest 4 mechs in view with a clear line.
Economy errors turn it off for the match. Dockerfile copies economy.py.

### DivyamBanga__buildathon 43c0fa1 11-20 23:39
Compare import state for modules imported on demand too; keep source readers through it
Expected practice score: ~153 s, anywhere from ~123 to ~188 (main at 765f19f:
~155 s; this branch adds the DuckDB stand-in and on-demand imports, about 2 s
of CPU on the board). Board anchor: e1fd283 scored 189.5 s = 170.3 s simulated
+ 19.2 s CPU over 40 commits. Not yet measured as a whole when committed.

Two places where the previous three commits meet 765f19f:

- wants_probe required a clean job. A class or module body change in a module
  the coordinator never imported is now checked in a child that imports the
  patched module on demand (a hot job), and it must go through the comparison
  of import state all the same: that is what narrows its candidates, and what
  notices that the module no longer imports when tests were left out by the
  class narrowing. The mode is no longer part of the test; a plan with only
  function bodies to swap has no import-time candidates and is not compared.
- finish_probe replaces the candidates by rest_candidates plus what the
  comparison leaves. Tests that read a changed source as a file are now in
  rest_candidates as well, so the comparison cannot drop them.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>

### DivyamBanga__buildathon 765f19f 11-20 23:38
Compare what an import-time change leaves behind; close five ways to miss a failing test
Expected practice score: ~155 s, anywhere from ~125 to ~190 (board-measured
so far: 189.5 s for e1fd283 = 170.3 s simulated + 19.2 s CPU).
Basis: on 240 commits generated like the organisers' sample (one token changed,
files chosen uniformly), 7 changed code that runs at import and were selected
wholesale at 25-37 s each; they now cost 0-2 s. That is about 0.9 s per commit,
so ~37 s over the 40 practice commits if they resemble that set, and nothing if
the practice set happens to hold no such commit.
Checked: 0 misses on the 30 sample commits, 205 mutants labeled with pytest
(two further labels, m01144 and m01158, are timeouts of the labeling run on an
overloaded machine: one is a comment-only patch, the other passes under pytest
on a calm machine), 21 of 160 new import-time mutants labeled so far, 13
labeled benchmark commits and 116 adversarial patches from an audit.

New: selector/state.py. A module or class body runs once, at import, and can
only leave the package in another state. A child imports the whole package
pinned and patched and compares the two results object by object. No
difference: nothing to select. A function with another default or closure:
the tests that run it. A constan

### DivyamBanga__buildathon e1fd283 11-20 21:22
Run one thing at a time: in-process pools, sequential children; complete case maps
Expected practice score: ~167 s (was ~173 s).
Basis: 30 sample commits on a quiet machine: 94.6 s simulated + 35.5 s CPU,
0 misses; practice = 1.175 x simulated + 1.586 x local CPU.
0 misses on 145 patches labeled with real pytest runs.

- The process pools the tests start are replaced by a stand-in that does the
  work in the test's own process, when its result is asked for (arguments and
  results are pickled as a pool would). No worker processes, and a failing
  test stops before the work it never looks at.
- Children run one at a time until the batch is 75 s in: two busy processes
  cost 10-15% more CPU for the same work.
- Per-case maps rebuilt from traces made with the fixed tracer (function
  first lines included); test costs measured again with the new runner.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>

### DivyamBanga__buildathon 4a0265c 11-20 20:52
Recognise more changes that cannot alter behaviour; compare code by resolved instructions
Expected practice score: ~173 s (same as 37c302e on the kinds seen so far;
this commit is about kinds the final may add).
Basis: 30 sample commits on a quiet machine: 100.8 s simulated + 33.9 s CPU,
0 misses; practice = 1.175 x simulated + 1.586 x local CPU.
0 misses on 117 patches labeled with real pytest runs.

- Code objects are compared as instructions with constants, names and jump
  targets resolved, so a constant table renumbered by the compiler (an edited
  annotation, a class moved onto a line number it also uses as a constant) is
  not mistaken for a change. Masking of unobservable constants is per use.
- A renamed local variable is not a change (parameters still are).
- A test file that only gains new tests, test classes or helper functions
  needs no test run.
- Module constants of the test helpers are narrowed to their readers.
- New mutant kinds for validation: docstrings, annotations, renames, new
  tests, import order.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>

### DivyamBanga__buildathon 37c302e 11-20 20:40
Harden against hostile patches: memory watchdog, CPU stall detection, unknown diffs
Expected practice score: ~173 s (unchanged in substance from c65dc5d).
Basis: 30 sample commits on a quiet machine: 100.8 s simulated + 34.1 s CPU,
0 misses; practice = 1.175 x simulated + 1.586 x local CPU (from the one
board result). 0 misses on 106 patches labeled with real pytest runs.

- A child that grows 1.2 GB past the coordinator is stopped (the run has 4 GB).
- A child burning CPU between tests (an import that loops) counts as stuck
  after 8 CPU seconds instead of 40 s of wall clock.
- A non-empty patch the parser does not recognise selects every test.
- Checked on synthetic worst cases: infinite loops in tests, in imports and
  in class bodies, unbounded allocation, os._exit, stack overflow, sleep,
  binary, renamed, deleted, new and non-applying files, pytest config edits.

### DivyamBanga__buildathon c65dc5d 11-20 20:34
Reuse recorded executor results for unchanged TPC queries
Expected practice score: ~175 s (was 194.7 s for 15ed632).
Basis: 30 sample commits on a quiet machine give 100.8 s simulated + 35.6 s
CPU, 0 misses; scaled by the one board result so far (practice simulated =
1.175 x sample simulated, practice CPU = 1.586 x local CPU).
Checked: 0 misses on the sample and on 96 patches labeled with real pytest runs.

- maps/execmemo.bin, execphase.json: what sqlglot's executor returns for each
  TPC query at the pinned commit, keyed by the optimized query, and every line
  that runs from planning to the result. For a patch that changes none of
  those lines, a query whose optimized form is unchanged is not executed again.
- The CPU cap per test uses the cost with nothing reused, so a test is not
  cut short because recorded results did not apply.
- Probes run whenever a check could become expensive.

### dmclaughlin-bit__mech-bot 69cdae0 11-21 05:25
Build 16: kill-value target selection
Replace nearest-clear targeting with a kill-value pick and a lock (target.ts).
Each enemy mech in view is scored on: a shot from here (clear line and a
weapon in range), time-to-kill from our weapon stats, low hp/max_hp, weak
weapons, and being alone (no other enemy within 40 m). The best one is locked
until it dies or has had no shot for 3 s. While the lock is briefly lost, any
other shootable enemy is shot without moving the lock. An enemy outside the
circle is picked only while we can shoot it from where we stand. Movement is
unchanged.

TARGET_PICK_ON in params.ts rolls back to Build 13 exactly (same actions as
origin/main on the kit recording, with and without a synthetic second enemy).
tools/target_check.ts counts targets, switches and picks offline.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>

### koillea__mech-royale-goonies cf8d2a4 11-21 02:57
C: intel tracking, cover when shot, fire back from the best angle
- intel.py: per-enemy estimates from sight, beams (exact shooter position), damage bearings (distance from a
  matching gunfire sound), incoming bullets, and sounds (footsteps, boost, jets, reloads, weapons);
  confidence decays (half-life 3 s); anonymous estimates merge by bearing and fold into seen mechs.
- Cover when shot (not before every fight, unlike v4): nearest spot hidden from the shooter and, per intel,
  from other mechs, preferring a firing spot toward the shooter on its back side and higher; hide (reload,
  regen, pre-aim), peek, duck back.
- Fixes for v4's likely failure modes: fight back against pushers (< 25 m) and flankers who see us in cover
  (< 70 m), stand and fight after 3 relocations in 6 s, zone always first.
- Pre-aim at heard threats; spot choice avoids places intel says are occupied.
- tests/test_intel.py, tests/test_combat.py.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01UyGDPGJgrZrQXhVBLhz6AQ

### koillea__mech-royale-goonies e8feab6 11-21 02:52
B: refined aim - motion prediction, pre-aim, rear-arc preference
- aim.py TargetTracker: 2 s history per target; steady movers use current velocity, strafers (2+ reversals
  across our line of sight) the window's drift velocity; airborne targets fall with gravity, never below
  ground; predictions never pass through walls. intercept() solves flight time against that prediction.
- Gun, laser and mortar aim through the tracker (decision latency included).
- Pre-aim: with no target, the torso tracks the nearest visible mech half a second ahead, or where a mech
  that hit us was heading after it hid (up to 2 s), instead of sweeping.
- Rear armour (x1.5, the game's only positional damage bonus): prefer targets facing away; 70 % of strafe
  legs walk around toward the target's back.
- tests/test_aim.py (10 cases).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01UyGDPGJgrZrQXhVBLhz6AQ

### kyoto-max__Mech_Royale 7723212 11-21 06:12
Phantom: hide in offline-computed low-exposure spots
Every survivor-family run scored 3.4-3.6 regardless of aim, firing or
weapons, so the score isn't decided by how we fight: we get found.
The map is identical every match, so visibility is precomputed:
- tools/exposure.py: for every standable 4 m cell, count viewers (8 m
  grid, eye +8 m, 200 m range) that can see a mech there, per protocol
  section 8 (buildings block; >3.5 m of tree crown blocks beyond 45 m).
  Writes exposure.u8 (2 m grid) and hideouts.json (440 spots).
- phantom profile: go straight to the lowest-exposure hideout inside
  the next circle, routing with an exposure cost; stand still; only
  shoot attackers or mechs within 45 m; burn the hideout and move when
  hit; loot only within 35 m; endgame (next radius <= 40) falls back
  to the survivor hold.
- climbs up to 40 m; per-turn compute slice 16 -> 12 ms.

### mike200004__mech-royale-bot 4321a00 11-20 22:12
Mech Royale bot v2 "hunter": kill-focused duelist
Rewrite of the decision logic around winning duels instead of hiding:
- loot plan: full-turn scan, best weapon pair (laser + lightning, else gun + one),
  drones and crates farmed for power cubes, kill drops collected, idle exploration
- only fights mechs that hunt us (approach, aim or damage), anything very close, or wounded
- per-loadout preferred distance, kites lightning carriers, rushes laser carriers with lightning
- exact lead for the gun (tick timing checked against recorded bullets), hitscan laser charge
  and release, lightning inside its cone, mortar ballistics with the barrel offset
- sidesteps visible bullets and shells, peeks from cover while weapons are down
- breaks off on a lost damage trade, regenerates behind cover, re-engages when healed
- zone handled by the time the closing wall needs to reach us
- tunable constants at the top of bot.py; time-capped planning (well under 50 ms per decision)
- stop tracking __pycache__

Local checks: kit check.py PASS (300/300 in time, p50 0.2 ms, max ~2.6 ms), extended smoke test
3600 synthetic observations with 0 invalid actions and no exceptions.

dead mech's track. Its stale track made the bot treat the place it died

is +4% max HP and +4% damage) and fewer upgrades.

### nshuai808__mech-royale c995b28 11-20 20:01
Add local logging harness: record, replay, analyze, botlog.trace
Matches show nothing but the score, so these stdlib-only tools give local
visibility into the bot:

- tools/record.py: transparent proxy around any bot command; logs every
  message, answer times, and botlog traces to replays/*.jsonl.gz
- tools/replay.py: feeds a recorded stream (default: the kit's 300 obs)
  to the bot lockstep, like the server; works inside the docker sandbox
- tools/analyze.py: report (timing, HP, zone, damage by weapon/attacker,
  rear hits, loot, modes, last seconds, timeline), CSV export, and --diff
  between two bot versions
- botlog.py: per-decision trace, off unless MECH_TRACE=1
- CLAUDE.md: game digest, tool usage, workflow, and status for new sessions
